De Luna, P., Hahn, C., Higgins, D., Jaffer, S.A., Jaramillo, T.F. and Sargent, E.H. (2019). What would it take for renewably powered electrosynthesis to displace petrochemical processes? Science 364(6438), eaav3506. doi:10.1126/science.aav3506 (Erratum 6 March 2020).

Locators are the article page numbers printed as "N of 9" (Table 1 p.2, Table 2 p.5). Review; most numbers are laboratory figures of merit or model results. Loaded: commercial PEM and alkaline water electrolyser energy conversion efficiency ranges (Table 1, reprinted from ref. 113); modelled production cost of electrocatalytic CO2 reduction to ethylene, CO, ethanol and formic acid (Table 2, assumptions in notes), with state of development. Not loaded (in _other-values): lab CO2-electrolyser figures of merit (Table 1), Table 2 life-cycle emissions and the bio/fossil comparators, FT and syngas-fermentation figures reprinted on p.6, competitiveness thresholds. Supplementary materials (tables S1-S3, fig. S2) not held. Traps: no price year (2019 used); electrocatalytic product costs are model outputs at assumed efficiencies and a 300 USD/kW electrolyser, not plant data; Table 2 emissions are cradle-to-grave at 0.295 kg CO2e/kWh grid, not scope 1; no TRLs printed anywhere.
